thread:
raj: Heads up — after last night's host-image + nvidia-toolkit flip, a handful of inference pods in apac-prod are crashing with libcuda/libnvidia-ml not found. Pods schedule but segfault at startup.
maria: Which nodes? any pattern by kernel/driver?
raj: Mostly g5.2xlarge-ish instances in ap-southeast-1. Some eu nodes are fine.
oliver: Seeing similar in canary region earlier but thought it was transient. Errors look like: 
```
Error loading shared library libcuda.so.1: No such file or directory (needed by /opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/libcudart.so)
/libcudnn.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
kai: Can you paste mount list from an affected host? suspect nvidia-container-toolkit hostbind not propagated into container mount namespace.
raj: Dumping quick output from node gpu-apac-04: 
```
$ mount | grep nvidia
/dev/nvidiactl on /usr/local/nvidia/driver type none (bind,ro,relatime)
/var/lib/nvidia on /usr/local/nvidia/lib type none (bind,ro,relatime)
```
But inside a container: 
```
# ls -l /usr/local/nvidia/lib
ls: cannot access '/usr/local/nvidia/lib': No such file or directory
```
maria: That smells like bind propagation mode changed to private/rprivate on the host during the image change. If host bind is rshared it appears in containers that join that mountns. If rprivate it won't.
oncall-lead: We rolled the baseimage that includes toolkit v1.13 and a permissive systemd tmpfiles change — could be the culprit. Rollback window?
raj: Rolling a hotfix: setting nvidia mounts to rshared on node init systemd unit and restarting kubelet on affected nodes. Doing one node now to validate.
oliver: Also seeing NCCL errors in jobs that managed to start: "NCCL error unhandled system error" — likely because /proc/driver/nvidia not populated. That explains inter-GPU comms failures after mount loss.
kai: For quick checks: run `nsenter --mount=/proc/1/ns/mnt -- mount | grep nvidia` on host and `kubectl exec -it pod -- ls /usr/local/nvidia` in container.
raj: Hotpatch applied to gpu-apac-04: restarted kubelet, re-created pods. Containers now see /usr/local/nvidia/lib and torch loads. Running a smoke infer test.
maria: Can we add an admission webhook to fail node images that change MS_PRIVATE flags? Might be heavy. Alternatively add a node-init systemd check to enforce rshared for /usr/local/nvidia and /var/lib/nvidia.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 - nvidia toolkit mount propagation regression (apac). Priority: high.
oncall-lead: Suggest we rollback the staged hostimage to previous sha in apac until we validate full fleet fix. Rolling back one ASG now slows drain. Cost impact: short-term extra oncall hours + potential job retries in apac.
raj: Agreed — starting rollback for ap-southeast-1 ASG-239. Will monitor GPU capacity; might need to shift some jobs to eu while we restore.
oliver: For postmortem angles: track which packaging change toggled mount propagation. The diff shows systemd unit changes around tmpfiles.d that now set PrivateTmp/PrivateMounts? Need to revert that part.
maria: Also add e2e canary to run a GPU container that validates presence of libcuda, /proc/driver/nvidia, and nvml before marking node healthy.
kai: Workaround for devs: add explicit copy of required libs into container image (ugly but will avoid runtime failure until fleet fix).
raj: Smoke test passed on patched node. Marking node healthy and bringing ASG back into rotation once rollback/patch completes.
maria: Thanks — please paste incident link and rollout plan when done.
raj: Incident: INC-2026-0421, rolling back apac now, ETA ~35m. Will post a short postmortem with root cause being mount propagation flag flip in host image upgrade. :white_check_mark:
